claims.statement: Finite validation randomness can affect even one selection; searching more noisy candidates can select a fortunate validation result, so the maximum alone does not establish independent improvement; retain search rules, candidates and attempt counts.
claims.scope: Methodological selection-bias risk; depends on candidate correlation, true quality and validation sample size. No claimed universal bias magnitude or guarantee of strictly increasing bias for duplicated identical candidates. Reporting advice makes selection auditable; it does not remove bias by itself.

evidence.supports: Finite-sample variance allows overfitting the model-selection criterion; the chosen sample optimum need not coincide with true optimum.
Maximizing a selection criterion can give an overly optimistic score.
Provides a bounded exact mechanism for increased opportunities to select favorable noise; not a new model result.
